signals.title: AUD/USD — G10 Bilateral Theme + Commodity-Linked Leader
signals.text: AUD leads the G10 board with a 1W average gain of +1.156% across 4 pairs, while USD lags at −0.860% across 9 pairs, establishing an outsized 2.016% bilateral spread. Fresh maritime mine strikes west of the Strait of Hormuz push WTI crude up +1.56% to $98.7/bbl, reinforcing broader commodity-linked FX demand. The policy backdrop aligns with this strength: RBA at 4.6% vs Fed 4.0% delivers a 60bp cash rate carry premium to AUD, corroborated by an overnight AONIA-SOFR spread of −72bp favoring AUD. Spot AUD/USD trades at 0.7020, clearing the 0.70223 swing resistance zone and holding above its SMA20 at 0.6979, though the 200-day average at 0.7051 leans against immediate upside. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; commodity support and positive carry favor continued outperformance. Catalyst: RBA meeting 3 Nov — hold bias priced. Risk: Strait of Hormuz tensions de-escalate sharply, unwinding the commodity risk premium.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Geopolitical Risk
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.72, holding above its SMA20/50 cluster at 158.00/157.65 within a range-bound structure below the SMA200 at 158.55. The 1M 25-delta risk reversal sits at −1.86, reflecting heavy demand for USD puts and downside protection against JPY appreciation. Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% maintains a 275bp policy rate advantage for the dollar (SOFR vs TONA spread at +265bp), but Strait of Hormuz military disruptions and equity softness in the Nikkei 225 (−2.06%) elevate geopolitical hedging flows. Leveraged funds hold net short JPY positions of −37,820 contracts (88th percentile of the 52-week range), leaving the carry trade vulnerable if headline shocks accelerate. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; severe options downside skew challenges nominal carry support. Catalyst: Japan Core CPI release today at 23:30 UTC. Risk: VIX remains suppressed near 16.7 and spot holds above the SMA50 at 157.65, allowing the carry grind to resume.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Retail Sentiment Extreme + ESI Divergence
signals.text: Retail sentiment data retail sentiment on USD/NOK sits at 100% long vs 0% short, registering a complete retail crowding extreme. This retail positioning directly opposes institutional flow: USD spec net long sits at +2,078 contracts while NOK benefits from a restrictive 4.5% policy rate vs Fed 4.0% (−50bp USD carry deficit). Norway's Economic Surprise Index registers a strong positive read at +17.2, supported by elevated energy revenues as WTI oil hits $98.7/bbl. USD/NOK spot trades at 9.361 in an active downtrend, trading entirely below its falling SMA20 (9.521) and SMA200 (9.522) while extended 2.03 ATR from its short-term mean. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK, contrarian to retail extreme. Catalyst: US Initial Jobless Claims at 12:30 UTC. Risk: US yields rebound sharply following today's 5-Year TIPS auction, forcing a technical short-covering squeeze toward 9.417.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Volatility Risk Premium + Positioning Crowding
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1246, remaining locked in an established downtrend below its SMA20 (1.1256), SMA50 (1.1453), and SMA200 (1.1581). Saxo Bank 1M ATM implied volatility trades at 6.6% against a 30-day realized volatility of 4.2%, creating an elevated vol risk premium of +2.5% that reflects significant hedging demand ahead of next week's policy meetings. CFTC data shows leveraged funds holding EUR net short positions of −92,833 contracts, sitting in the 4th percentile of the 52-week range (z = −1.78σ) after a WoW reduction of −8,058 contracts. Carry heavily penalizes the single currency, with Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% driving a 135bp spread in favor of the dollar (€STR vs SOFR spread at +144bp). Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; persistent carry disadvantage and structural downtrend cap rallies. Catalyst: ECB policy meeting 29 Oct — hold priced. Risk: Crowded institutional shorts cover on fiscal or political de-escalation in Europe, driving a short squeeze back above the SMA20 at 1.1256.
